test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-6) Official paper (Held On: 9 May 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: ABCD is a rectangle with AB = 10 cm and BC = 8 cm. O is the centre of a circle touching the three sides AB, BC and CD of the rectangle ABCD. Find the area (in cm²) of ΔOBC.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The circle touches the parallel sides **AB** and **CD** of the rectangle.

Diameter of the circle = Distance between **AB** and **CD** = **BC** = 8 cm.

Radius (r) of the circle = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm.

In Δ**OBC**, the base is **BC** = 8 cm and the height (altitude from **O**) is the radius = 4 cm.

Area of Δ**OBC** = 1/2 × base × height = 1/2 × 8 × 4 = 16 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 16 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **AB** = 10 cm, **BC** = 8 cm. Circle touches **AB**, **BC**, and **CD**.

**Formula:** Area of Triangle = 1/2 × base × height.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/377a5ea36502d09cd77d7d8bda3048c2893b576a030dde3a58de11f407031a25.png] 

⇒ In rectangle **ABCD**, side **AB** is parallel to **CD**.

⇒ The distance between **AB** and **CD** is **BC** = 8 cm.

⇒ Since the circle touches **AB** and **CD**, its diameter = 8 cm.

⇒ Radius of the circle (r) = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm.

⇒ The circle also touches side **BC**, so the distance from the center **O** to **BC** is the radius.

⇒ In Δ**OBC**, let base = **BC** = 8 cm.

⇒ Height of Δ**OBC** = Distance from **O** to **BC** = radius = 4 cm.

⇒ Area of Δ**OBC** = 1/2 × 8 × 4

⇒ Area of Δ**OBC** = 4 × 4 = 16 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 16 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Inscribed Circles

When a circle touches two parallel lines, its diameter is equal to the perpendicular distance between those lines.

Area of Triangle

The area of any triangle is calculated as 1/2 × base × height, where the height is the perpendicular distance from the opposite vertex to the base line.

Rectangle Geometry

In a rectangle **ABCD**, opposite sides are equal and parallel (**AB** = **CD** and **BC** = **AD**), and all interior angles are 90°.</p
